header: Recommended CloudWatch alarms for Amazon OpenSearch Service
content:
Service
CloudWatch alarms perform an action when a CloudWatch metric exceeds a speciﬁed value for
some amount of time. For example, you might want AWS to email you if your cluster health status
Use UltraWarm and cold storage for time-series log data
1848
Amazon OpenSearch Service
Developer Guide
is red for longer than one minute. This section includes some recommended alarms for Amazon
OpenSearch Service and how to respond to them.
You can automatically deploy these alarms using CloudFormation. For a sample stack, see the
related GitHub repository.
Note
If you deploy the CloudFormation stack, the KMSKeyError and KMSKeyInaccessible
alarms will exists in an Insufficient Data state because these metrics only appear if a
domain encounters a problem with its encryption key.
For more information about conﬁguring alarms, see Creating Amazon CloudWatch Alarms in the
Amazon CloudWatch User Guide.

An automated snapshot failed. This failure is often the result of a red
cluster health status. See the section called “Red cluster status”.
For a summary of all automated snapshots and some information

GET domain_endpoint /_snapshot/cs-automated/_all

80% for 1 minute, 3

The cluster could encounter out of memory errors if usage increases
. Consider scaling vertically. OpenSearch Service uses half of an
instance's RAM for the Java heap, up to a heap size of 32 GiB. You can
scale instances vertically up to 64 GiB of RAM, at which point you can
scale horizontally by adding instances.

The total number of active primary and replica shards is greater than
30,000. You might be rotating your indexes too frequently. Consider
using ISM to remove indexes once they reach a speciﬁc age.
